title: feat(notifications): the push channel — service-push (APNs + FCM) and its channel shell in service-messaging
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8MDJvNuJodyHTc3YS13avjC)_
Fixes #29041

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

1. 改了什么：通知现在能推送到手机。新增推送服务包 `@objectstack/service-push`（苹果 APNs、谷歌 FCM），消息服务新增“推送”渠道：流程里的通知节点选了推送，就发到收件人登记过的每一台手机，点开推送进入这条通知对应的页面；手机端应用已卸载（令牌失效）时，自动停用那台设备。同时修订 ADR-0012（通知平台）：推送包名定为 `service-push`，§4 推送一行改为“已上线”，§6 写明失效令牌由推送渠道停用；ADR-0030 未改。
2. 为什么改：#29041 的验收条件。之前流程里选了推送也显示“运行成功”，实际一条推送都没有发出（已在 main 上复现）。
3. 风险与回滚：纯新增。没有启用推送服务的部署，行为完全不变；推送密钥只能通过引用（`credentialRef`）配置，写明文密钥会在启动时被拒绝；推送里带的跳转只会是本服务器内的路径，外站链接一律不带。回滚即还原本 PR。
4. 先看：`packages/services/service-messaging/src/push-channel.ts`（发给哪些手机、失效设备停用、结果怎么分级），再看 `docs/adr/0012-notification-platform.md` 的修订处。
5. 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/builtin/notify-push-delivery.integration.test.ts`，预期 3 条全过：模拟的苹果和谷歌推送服务各收到一条带跳转的推送，被报失效的设备变为停用，同一用户的另一台手机照常收到。
6. 需要你做的：席位契约复核已通过（评论 6596752211，`Head-sha: 3aac0c5938b09d8b7a6cb7ffa88507dca5ec7cfb`），请批准 ADR-0012（通知平台）的这次修订。本 PR 属于 Tier H 就是因为它，只改了状态行的 `Amended` 说明和 §4、§6 两处。

## What changes

- **New package `@objectstack/service-push`** (`packages/services/service-push`, named per the maintainer's 2026-11-03 ruling: kernel services are `service-*`). `PushServicePlugin` registers the kernel's `push` service, an `IPushService` with one transport per configured vendor:
  - `ApnsPushTransport`: APNs over HTTP/2 (`node:http2`, one held session) with token-based auth. An ES256 provider token is signed with the `.p8` key and reused for fifty minutes (APNs refuses one older than an hour and throttles refreshes under twenty). `200` is sent; `BadDeviceToken` / `Unregistered` / `410` is `invalid_token`; `ExpiredProviderToken` re-signs once; `429` / `5xx` are retryable; other refusals are not. A token that is not hex is answered `invalid_token` and never reaches the request path.
  - `FcmPushTransport`: FCM HTTP v1. An RS256 assertion signed with the service account's key is exchanged for an OAuth access token, kept until a minute before expiry. `UNREGISTERED` (or `404 NOT_FOUND`) is `invalid_token`; a `401` refreshes the token once; `429` / `5xx` are retryable.
  - Configuration is the plugin's `config` option, parsed with `PushServiceConfigSchema` at init, so an inline secret or a misspelt key fails the boot with the schema's guidance. Each secret is a `credentialRef`, resolved when the transport first signs through `resolveCredential` (default: the open tier's rule, the name of an environment variable; ADR-0143 D3). No error or log line carries a secret or a whole device token.
- **`@objectstack/service-messaging`: the `push` channel shell** (`push-channel.ts`), mounted through the same lazy provider as the sms channel, so it is present exactly while a `push` service is registered. One delivery reaches every enabled device of the recipient on a vendor the service can reach. The push carries the notification's title and body (already in the recipient's language) and the delivery data `PushDeliveryDataSchema` declares: `notificationId`, plus `route` when the notification's `actionUrl` passes `PushRouteSchema` (an off-server, dot-segment or encoded path is left out; the delivery still goes). Title and body are cut to 256 / 2048 UTF-8 bytes so the payload stays under the vendors' 4 KB.
  - A token reported dead is retired through `invalidateDeviceToken` (row kept, `enabled: false`, `invalidatedAt`); the user's other devices still get the push.
  - Grades: one device pushed ⇒ delivered (a failure beside it is logged, not retried, so no device is pushed twice); every device dead, or no enabled device ⇒ `invalid_recipient` (suppressed); devices only on an unconfigured vendor, or a refusal no retry repairs ⇒ `permanent`; timeout / `429` / `5xx` with nothing delivered ⇒ `retryable`; no push service ⇒ refused `transport_not_configured`, as the sms and email channels refuse it. `isAvailable` answers from the push service's vendors, no I/O.
- **Who owns `sys_user_device`** (contract-review item 3 of 6593642547): service-messaging owns it; its push channel reads it and retires tokens in it; service-push never touches it. `user-device.object.ts` and `push-device.zod.ts` now say the same.
- **`packages/spec`: PLANNED flips and text only.** The `[PLANNED — not yet read]` markers come off `PushServiceConfigSchema` / `ApnsTransportConfigSchema` / `FcmTransportConfigSchema` and `[PLANNED — not yet served]` off `PushDeliveryDataSchema` (their reader and producer ship here); the two marker pins flip to "no PLANNED marker". `push-config.zod.ts`'s docblock names `@objectstack/service-push` where it named `plugin-notification-push`. `NotificationChannelSchema`'s JSDoc lists `push` among the registered channels (Wanted 7 of #29067). The three items of 6593642547: the `NOT_FOUND` synonym waiver's reason names service-messaging's provenance row; `INotificationService`'s device comments say the push channel reads `listDevices` and calls `invalidateDeviceToken` (true as of this PR); the ownership sentence above. Reference pages regenerated (`push-config.mdx`, `push-delivery.mdx`). No key, shape or export changes.
- **ADR-0012** (superseded by ADR-0030, which is unchanged): the status line gains `Amended (2026-11-03, #29041)`: push ships as `service-push` plus the channel shell in service-messaging, which owns `sys_user_device`, and every `plugin-notification-push` in the ADR reads that way. §4's push row names the shipped packages; §6 records that the channel, not the dispatcher, retires the dead token (one delivery fans out to several devices) and that the shipped device shape is `system/push-device.zod.ts`; the domestic-vendor package name no longer coins a `plugin-` name.
- Docs and registration: `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx` (service count 17 → 18, a `service-push` entry, the messaging line), `CONTRIBUTING.md` package row, `.changeset/config.json` fixed group, `packages/spec/llms.txt` package count 73 → 74 (forced by `check:llms-txt`; prose in the spec tree, not a schema), README.
- Changeset `.changeset/29041-push-notification-channel.md`: `service-push`, `service-messaging` and `spec` all `patch` (`Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, ruling A on #25105).

## Why

#29041 asks that a `notify` node deliver a push to a registered device through APNs/FCM, carry `route`, and retire a token reported invalid. The protocol face (#29067, PR #29218) and the device registry (#29068, PR #29628) had landed; nothing sent.

## Tests

- **Red first, on `origin/main` `7b55ea95`** (a throwaway probe, not committed): a `notify` node with `channels: ['push']` over the real `MessagingService` with a registered APNs device and a local HTTP/2 server → `run.success: true`, `summary.acted: 0`, `APNS requests received: 0`; the probe's `expect(received).toHaveLength(1)` failed.
- **Acceptance** `service-automation/src/builtin/notify-push-delivery.integration.test.ts` (3): the node delivers to an iOS and an Android device through mock APNs (HTTP/2) and mock Google (OAuth + FCM v1) with the real transports, `route` and `notificationId` in both payloads; the source record's `/OBJECT/ID` rides as `route` when no url is given; a token APNs answers `410 Unregistered` is retired (`enabled: false`, `invalidatedAt` set), the other device still gets the push, and the retired device is not pushed again.
- `service-push` (30): APNs request shape and an ES256 token the public key verifies, dead-token reasons, re-sign on `ExpiredProviderToken`, token reuse for fifty minutes, retryable vs not, unresolved and unusable credentials never echoed and never sent, a non-hex token never in the path; FCM assertion verified with the public key, message shape, `UNREGISTERED`, access-token reuse and 401 refresh, retryable vs not, bad service account, token-endpoint refusal; plugin config parse, inline-secret refusal at init, host transport override, masked token in logs, the env resolver.
- `service-messaging/src/push-channel.test.ts` (14): device selection, data shape against `PushDeliveryDataSchema`, off-server routes left out, dead-token retirement with the other device still pushed, every grade above, byte truncation, `isAvailable`, and the plugin mount: refused before a `push` service exists, delivered through it once registered.
- Ablations (each restored, blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty; `ablation-replace.mjs` under a trap): the `invalidateDeviceToken` call removed → `push-channel.test.ts` 2 failed of 14 (the two retirement cases); `PushRouteSchema.safeParse(actionUrl).success` replaced by `true` → 1 failed of 14 (the off-server route case).
- Forced test edits: `push-config.test.ts` and `push-delivery.test.ts` marker pins flip from "carries the PLANNED marker" to "carries no PLANNED marker".

## Acceptance notes

- **No served door yet.** Push is configured only where a host composes `new PushServicePlugin({ config })`. `os serve` has no `push` capability (`packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`) and the stack definition no `config.push` key, so a served deployment cannot switch push on from its configuration. Both are spec edits outside this card's surface; named for the seat to card (a capability token, a stack door and a `resolvePushCapabilityArg` beside `resolveSmsCapabilityArg`).
- **Text is the recipient's, not the device's.** The push sends the notification's title and body as fan-out rendered them for the recipient (`sys_user.locale`, else the deployment default), the same text the inbox row shows. `UserDeviceSchema.locale`'s description says pushes to the device are rendered in the device locale; nothing reads it. Reported to the seat.
- **No push template.** `sys_notification_template` accepts `email` and `sms` only (`TEMPLATE_CHANNELS`), so there is no per-topic push template; widening it is not this card.
- A delivery with one device pushed and another failing retryably is recorded delivered and not retried, on purpose: a retry would push the delivered devices again.
- HMS / Xiaomi / OPPO / vivo stay out of scope (ADR-0012 §6), as does a hosted configuration surface (triage 6570782253).

## Verification

Readings above. The PR stays a draft; the seat runs the contract review on the spec marker face.
